blogs.title: The Reasonable Observer Prevails: Why Santos’s Subjective Intent Failed the Fair Use Test
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Second Circuit's application of the transformative use doctrine in Santos v. Kimmel, specifically focusing on the court's rejection of the plaintiff's argument that his subjective intent in creating the videos controls the fair use analysis. We examine how the court relied on Andy Warhol Found. v. Goldsmith to prioritize the 'reasonable observer' standard over the copyright holder's original purpose, and discuss the implications for the 'bad faith' argument derived from Harper & Row.

blogs.title: Beyond Copyright: Why Privity and Pleading Standards Doomed Santos’s State Law Claims
blogs.description: While the copyright ruling grabs headlines, this post dissects the dismissal of Santos's state law claims for breach of contract and fraudulent inducement. We explore the court's application of Illinois law regarding third-party beneficiaries under the Cameo Terms of Service, the failure to allege essential terms under New York implied contract law, and the strict out-of-pocket loss requirement for fraud claims in New York.

blogs.title: Early Dismissal of Fair Use: Is the Second Circuit Lowering the Bar for 12(b)(6) Motions?
blogs.description: This post considers the procedural significance of affirming a Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal based on the affirmative defense of fair use. By citing Hachette and TCA Television, the Second Circuit reinforces the viability of resolving fair use at the pleading stage when the facts are clear. We discuss what this trend means for copyright litigation strategy and the burden on defendants to plead transformative use.
